Le tableau qui sert à ce calcul porte le: The grid used for this calculation is named after Reginald Punnett, who devised it in 1905, a few years after Mendel's rediscovery. The first published diagrams date from 1906.
L'article de Watson et Crick paraît dans: Watson and Crick's paper appeared in Nature on 25 April 1953, barely two pages long. It contains a famous understatement: "It has not escaped our notice" that this pairing suggests how DNA is copied.
À la fin des années 1940, le biochimiste: In the late 1940s, biochemist Erwin Chargaff measured that there is always as much adenine as thymine, and as much guanine as cytosine. These "Chargaff's rules" guided Watson and Crick.
Walther Flemming publie à partir de 1878: Walther Flemming published his observations of cell division from 1878 onwards, gathering them in a book in 1882. He named "chromatin" the material that takes up dyes; Wilhelm von Waldeyer later named chromosomes.
Francis Galton utilise les jumeaux pour: Francis Galton used twins to untangle nature and nurture in the late 19th century. But it was only in 1924 that Hermann Siemens clearly distinguished identical from fraternal twins.
En 1905, la biologiste américaine Nettie: In 1905, American biologist Nettie Stevens discovered in the mealworm a small chromosome, the future Y, whose presence decides sex. Edmund Wilson, working in parallel, long received the credit alone.
En 1926, Hermann Muller montre que les r: In 1926, Hermann Muller showed that X-rays cause mutations in fruit flies. Awarded the Nobel Prize in 1946, he went on to warn about the dangers of fallout from nuclear tests.
Avant le projet Génome humain, lancé en: Before the Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, our gene count was estimated at 80,000 to 140,000. The project, declared complete on 14 April 2003, found far fewer: about 20,000 protein-coding genes.
Le prix récompense un article de 2012 da: The prize rewarded a 2012 paper in Science, in which Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed that Cas9 can be guided by an RNA to cut DNA wherever one wants.
La Fabrica de Vésale, parue en 1543 quan: Vesalius's Fabrica, published in 1543 when he was 28, opens with the skeleton, which he saw as the framework of the body. Its plates come from human, not animal, dissections.
Harvey publie De motu cordis en 1628 à F: Harvey published De motu cordis in 1628 in Frankfurt, home of a major book fair. One critic wrote that he would "rather err with Galen than proclaim the truth with Harvey": it took about twenty years for the idea to be accepted.
En 1661, Marcello Malpighi observe au mi: In 1661, Marcello Malpighi looked at frog lungs under the microscope: he discovered capillaries and described the alveoli, which he compared to the holes of a honeycomb.
Dès 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld décrit le r: As early as 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld described haemoglobin's role in carrying oxygen. In 1959, Max Perutz worked out its structure, earning him the 1962 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Dans la médecine d'Hippocrate puis de Ga: In the medicine of Hippocrates and later Galen, yellow bile and black bile were two of the body's four "humours", along with blood and phlegm. This theory dominated Western medicine for more than 2,000 years.
En 1602, le médecin italien Santorio San: In 1602, Italian physician Santorio Santorio invented the pulsilogium, an instrument to measure the pulse, probably the first precision machine in the history of medicine.
Le 30 juillet 1921 à Toronto, Banting et: On 30 July 1921 in Toronto, Banting and Best lowered a diabetic dog's blood sugar with a pancreatic extract. In January 1922, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson became the first patient treated.
Le mythe des 10 % circule dès les années: The 10% myth was circulating by the 1920s in self-help books. In 1936, the foreword to a Dale Carnegie bestseller wrongly attributed it to psychologist William James.
Vesalius was 28 when the Fabrica came out. He then left Padua, where he had taught since 1537, to become a physician at the imperial court of Charles V.
En 1628, William Harvey calcule que le c: In 1628, William Harvey calculated that the heart pumps about 225 kg of blood a day, more than the body's weight, even with low estimates. So the liver cannot be making all that blood, as Galen believed: blood goes round in a loop.
Les petits filtres du rein portent le no: The kidney's small filters bear the name of Marcello Malpighi, the Italian anatomist who named them. He also discovered blood capillaries in 1661.
C'est Jenner qui forge en 1798 l'express: It was Jenner who coined the phrase Variolae vaccinae, "smallpox of the cow", in 1798. In 1881, Louis Pasteur proposed calling all protective inoculations "vaccines", in Jenner's honour.
Fleming découvre la pénicilline en septe: Fleming discovered penicillin in September 1928, a substance that kills bacteria. In his 1945 Nobel lecture, he already warned that a patient who underdoses himself can make microbes resistant.
En 1898, Martinus Beijerinck appelle l'a: In 1898, Martinus Beijerinck called the tobacco mosaic agent a contagium vivum fluidum, a "contagious living fluid", and named it a virus. In 1935, Wendell Stanley crystallised it: it is a particle, not a liquid.
Le « B » des lymphocytes B vient de la b: The "B" of B cells comes from the bursa of Fabricius, an organ found in birds, not from bone marrow. They were discovered there in chickens, in a 1956 paper.
Semmelweis ne sait pas expliquer pourquo: Semmelweis could not explain why washing worked, and his colleagues rejected him. Committed to an asylum in 1865, he died fourteen days later; today he is called the "saviour of mothers".
En 1885, Louis Pasteur, chimiste et non: In 1885, Louis Pasteur, a chemist rather than a doctor, inoculated Joseph Meister, aged 9, who had been bitten by a dog believed to be rabid. The boy did not develop rabies; as an adult, he became caretaker of the Pasteur Institute.
Robert Koch annonce sa découverte le 24: Robert Koch announced his discovery on 24 March 1882 in Berlin, to a small group of scientists. That date has become World Tuberculosis Day.
Le dernier cas naturel de variole est Al: The last natural case of smallpox was Ali Maow Maalin, a hospital cook in Merca, Somalia, in October 1977. After recovering, he went on to vaccinate children against polio.
L'expression « immunité de troupeau » vi: The phrase "herd immunity" comes from vets: American Daniel Elmer Salmon used it as early as 1894 for herds of pigs. It moved on to human diseases in the late 1920s.
En 1868, le médecin allemand Carl Wunder: In 1868, German physician Carl Wunderlich set normal temperature at 37 °C and stated that "fever is not a disease, but a symptom". Today the average is estimated a little lower, around 36.8 °C.
En 1880, à l'hôpital militaire de Consta: In 1880, at the military hospital in Constantine, Algeria, Alphonse Laveran discovered the malaria parasite in a patient's blood (Nobel 1907). Ronald Ross proved the mosquito's role in 1898.
En 1940, avant même que la pénicilline s: In 1940, even before penicillin was used on patients, Abraham and Chain isolated from E. coli an enzyme that destroys it, penicillinase. Resistance already existed in nature.
En 1779, Jan Ingenhousz montre que les p: In 1779, Jan Ingenhousz showed that plants only "restore" spoiled air in sunlight: the first glimpse of photosynthesis, the engine of all producers.
Le dernier livre scientifique de Darwin,: Darwin's last scientific book, published in October 1881, is about earthworms and how they recycle soil. Thousands of copies sold within weeks.
Haeckel forge le mot dans un livre de 18: Haeckel coined the word in an 1866 book, General Morphology of Organisms. He took it from the Greek oikos, house: ecology is the study of living things' "home".
La règle des 10 % vient de Raymond Linde: The 10% rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in a 1942 paper based on his thesis about a small lake in Minnesota. First rejected as "too generalized", it was published thanks to Hutchinson's support; Lindeman died aged 26.
Les derniers loups de Yellowstone avaien: Yellowstone's last wolves had been killed in 1926. In March 1995, 14 wolves captured in Canada were released in the Lamar Valley, then 17 more in 1996.
Dès 1856, l'Américaine Eunice Foote mont: As early as 1856, American Eunice Foote showed that carbon dioxide and water vapour trap heat from the sun. In 1859, John Tyndall measured their absorption of infrared and proved the greenhouse effect experimentally.
Robert Paine retire les étoiles de mer d: Robert Paine removed starfish from a rocky shore at Makah Bay, in the United States: mussels took over, and 15 species fell to 8 in three years. In 1969 he drew from it the idea of a keystone species.
Printemps silencieux paraît le 27 septem: Silent Spring came out on 27 September 1962, and the chemical industry attacked Rachel Carson even before its release. The United States banned DDT for farm use in 1972.
Le premier blanchissement massif reconnu: The first mass bleaching recognised worldwide dates from 1998: in the Indian Ocean, 80% of corals bleached and 20% died. In 2016, it killed 29 to 50% of the Great Barrier Reef's corals.
En mars 1958, Charles David Keeling comm: In March 1958, Charles David Keeling began measuring carbon dioxide in the air atop Mauna Loa, Hawaii: 313 ppm. By November 2018, the curve had reached 406 ppm.
En 1958, l'écologue anglais Charles Elto: In 1958, English ecologist Charles Elton published The Ecology of Invasions by Animals and Plants, the first book to warn about the damage done by invasive species. He was the one who had introduced the food chain in 1927.
Le chiffre de 31 % vient des évaluations: The 31% figure comes from the FAO's global forest assessments. Between 1990 and 2020, the world's forests lost 178 million hectares, but net loss slowed: 7.8 million hectares a year in the 1990s, 4.7 million in 2010-2020.
Mullis fait la démonstration de la PCR l: Mullis demonstrated PCR on 16 December 1983, at Cetus in California, and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. It became practical thanks to the enzyme of a bacterium found in 1969 in a Yellowstone hot spring.
Les drôles de répétitions de l'ADN qu'on: The odd DNA repeats now called CRISPR were first described in 1987 in the bacterium E. coli, by a Japanese team. Nobody then knew what they were for.
Dolly naît le 5 juillet 1996 à l'Institu: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute, in Scotland, after 277 attempts. Cloned from a mammary gland cell, she was named after the singer Dolly Parton.
Katalin Karikó a longtemps travaillé sur: Katalin Karikó worked on messenger RNA for years without funding: her university demoted her in 1995. Her 2005 discovery with Drew Weissman, rejected by Nature and Science, won them the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
L'insuline humaine fabriquée par génie g: Human insulin made by genetic engineering, developed by Genentech in 1978 and sold by Eli Lilly as Humulin, was approved in 1982: the first genetically engineered medicine.
Lancé officiellement en 1990, le projet: Officially launched in 1990, the Human Genome Project was declared complete on 14 April 2003, two years ahead of schedule. It cost about $2.7 billion, less than the expected $3 billion.
Le premier OGM est une bactérie rendue r: The first GMO was a bacterium made resistant to an antibiotic by Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen in 1973. Then came the transgenic mouse in 1974 and the Flavr Savr tomato, the first GM food sold, in 1994.
En 1988, Colin Pitchfork devient le prem: In 1988, Colin Pitchfork became the first murderer convicted thanks to his DNA profile, for two murders in Leicestershire. An earlier suspect, who had confessed, was innocent.
En 2006, Shinya Yamanaka transforme des: In 2006, Shinya Yamanaka turned adult mouse cells into stem cells with just four genes, then human cells in 2007. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize with John Gurdon.
La découverte clé de Karikó et Weissman,: Karikó and Weissman's key discovery, in 2005, was to replace uridine in RNA with pseudouridine so it no longer alarms the immune system. It won them the Nobel Prize in Medicine, announced on 2 October 2023.
En 2005, on comprend que les morceaux d': In 2005, it was understood that the DNA fragments stored in CRISPR come from viruses that attacked the bacterium. Experimental proof of this bacterial immune system came in 2007.
En 1974, les chercheurs du monde entier: In 1974, researchers worldwide paused their recombinant DNA experiments until an international conference could be held. Asilomar brought together about 140 participants in February 1975, mostly biologists, but also lawyers and doctors.
